messages:
Anna Park: Kicking off PRD thread for Dedicated Serving autoscale + SLA playbook. Draft here: https://redwood.atlassian.com/prd/dedicated-autoscale (high level). Need acceptance criteria, concrete sizing, and rollout gating. Customer asks: predictable p95 latency for reserved pools + graceful burst handling. Thoughts?

Jeremy Liu: Thanks — quick questions up front: do we split SLAs by request class (short vs long)? I think we should. Also we need explicit throughput targets (tokens/s or req/s) per pool size to size commits.

Mike Torres: From infra POV we should define classes. Proposal: short (<=512 tokens), medium (513-2048), long (>2048). Suggested steady-state SLOs: short p95 <= 120ms, medium p95 <= 300ms, long p95 <= 800ms. Note: long requests often exceed these on large models; we can offer separate expectations for model families.

Sophia Patel: Draft acceptance criteria (brain dump):
- End-to-end latency SLOs per class met in 95% of production windows for committed pools.
- Autoscale triggers correctly within thresholds and maintains SLOs during 30m synthetic load tests.
- Canary rollout shows no more than 5% latency regression vs baseline and error rate <0.5%.
- Failover path: when capacity constrained, 100% of traffic for affected routes falls back to a validated quantized/cheaper variant with no data loss.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost and p95/p99 latency dashboards available.

Jeremy Liu: We need concrete autoscale rules and metric names. How do we measure "queue depth" and what thresholds? Also, what cooldowns for scale-down to avoid thrash?

Mike Torres: Metric names and thresholds (proposal):
- Metrics: `serving.queue_depth`, `runtime.gpu_utilization`, `route.inflight_requests`, `route.p95_latency`
- Scale-up: if `serving.queue_depth > 50` for 30s OR `runtime.gpu_utilization > 85%` for 60s -> add instance(s).
- Scale-down: `serving.queue_depth == 0` AND `runtime.gpu_utilization < 40%` for 10m -> remove instance(s) (respect min_pool_size).
- Warm pool: maintain `min_warm_nodes` per pool (default 1) to avoid cold-starts.
- Burst policy: allow up to 2x burst from shared buffer for <= 2 minutes; after that, enforce queuing or autoscale.

Sophia Patel: Nice. For rollout/gating I suggest: alpha with 2 enterprise customers (opt-in), canary split 10% for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then 100%. Gate passes if: error rate < 0.5%, latency regression < 10% relative to baseline, no increase in dropped requests.

Jeremy Liu: Edge cases we need to capture in PRD: noisy neighbor (one tenant saturates GPUs), cold KV cache after deploy, sudden model sequence-length spikes (customer sends extremely long prompts), storage I/O spikes causing slowdowns. For each: define mitigation and acceptance test.

Anna Park: Agreed. Mitigations: per-tenant token buckets + per-route priority; KV cache warmers during rollout; preflight checks reject sequences > max_seq unless explicit flag; fallback to smaller model variant automatically if route.p95 exceeds threshold for > 2m.

Mike Torres: Implementation sketch (autoscale policy snippet):
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  scale_up:
    - condition: serving.queue_depth > 50 for 30s
    - condition: runtime.gpu_utilization > 85% for 60s
  scale_down:
    - condition: queue_depth == 0 and gpu_utilization < 40% for 10m
  warm_pool: min_warm_nodes: 1
  burst: max_multiplier: 2 window: 120s
```

Sophia Patel: Launch playbook notes:
- Preflight: run synthetic load that mirrors customer mix (short:60%, medium:30%, long:10%) for 24h.
- Canary: 10% traffic -> monitor metrics for 48h.
- Rollback triggers: rate increase > 0.5pp, p95 regression > 10% for 15m, or SLO miss > 1% in 30m.

Anna Park: Cost and packaging: reserved pools come with base SLOs. Offer "pre-warm" add-on (extra monthly fee) to raise `min_warm_nodes` to reduce cold starts. Burst capacity above committed level can be billable. Need pricing appendix in PRD.

Jeremy Liu: Testing/acceptance checklist (short):
- Unit + integration tests for autoscale conditions.
- Canary harness that can replay customer traffic slices.
- Regression evals against prompt set (no semantic regressions when falling back to cheaper variants).
- Chaos test: kill node during spike, expect no >1% client-visible errors.

Sophia Patel: Final acceptance criteria (to include in PRD):
1) For committed pools, short requests p95 <= 120ms and medium p95 <= 300ms during 95% of 30-day windows.
2) Autoscale maintains SLOs under synthetic bursts and recovers within target time (scale-up within 2 min for sustained load).
3) Canary rollout gating metrics met (error rate <0.5%, latency regression <10%).
4) Graceful degradation path exists and preserves correctness (fallback model variant verified).
5) Observability and customer-facing SLA docs published.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: 2025-09-02T15:00:00Z -> 10% traffic (tag: dedicated-autoscale-v1).

Mike Torres: Also adding ops runbook entry: how to manually force warm nodes, how to drain without dropping requests, and steps to revert model variant routing. I'll add PR to infra-runbooks.

Anna Park: Great set of inputs — I'll merge into PRD draft and tag owners for each acceptance criterion. Please drop any objections here by EOD. :thumbsup:
